item.title: Weighted Views Representation with Multi-Head Coulomb Attention for Molecular Property Prediction
item.description:
Abstract
We extend the weighted-views molecular featurization framework (d’Avezac, Botts, Mohlenkamp, and Zunger, 2011) by enriching it with single-atom properties and Coulomb pair information. We use these enriched views within a machine-learning architecture incorporating shared Transformers whose attention scores directly incorporate Coulomb interactions, weighted aggregation of view outputs, and a final prediction neural network. We demonstrate performance competitive with the state-of-the-art on the QM7 atomization energy benchmark (regression), ranking enantiomers by their docking scores (trained as regression, tested by ranking), lipophilicity (regression), and blood–brain barrier penetration (classification).

item.title: Retraction of “ Toxicity of Nanoscaled Zero-Valent Iron Particles on Tilapia, Oreochromis mossambicus ”
item.description: The authors retract “Toxicity of Nanoscaled Zero-Valent Iron Particles on Tilapia, Oreochromis mossambicus” (DOI: 10.1021/acsomega.2c05696) because there is overlap between panels A, B and C in Figure 4, indicating that the images were taken from the same sample. The authors provided image files during the post-publication review process; however, sufficient confidence in the relationship of the data to the results reported in the article was not assured. This undermines the reliability of the results presented. As such, the article is being retracted.

Abstract
We present a differential-geometric formulation of chemical reaction dynamics in which the nuclear configuration space is treated as a curved manifold whose metric is induced by the covariant Hessian of the potential energy surface (PES). In this Riemannian setting, reaction pathways emerge as geodesics of a curvature-weighted action, providing an intrinsic, coordinate-independent alternative to steepest-descent and chain-of-states methods. The second variation of the action δ2S furnishes a rigorous stability index that identifies transition states as regions of negative sectional curvature and links vibrational structure directly to curvature eigenvalues through the Jacobi operator. The transition state (TS) corresponds intrinsically to a region where the manifold’s signature becomes pseudo-Riemannian, characterized by local instability where δ2S < 0. Furthermore, the linearization of the geodesic equation yields a Jacobi operator, whose eigenvalues reproduce harmonic and anharmonic vibrational frequencies, directly connecting spectroscopic data to curvature invariants. Applied to the dissociation channels of water (H2O → H + OH) and (H2O → H2 + O), this framework reproduces fundamental vibrational frequencies, rotational constants, and anharmonicities with 1–5% accuracy and generates detailed stability maps that resolve hyperbolic, parabolic, and elliptic regions along the minimal path. Beyond reproducing known mechanistic information, the formalism reveals geometric features─channel anisotropy, curvature-driven bifurcations, and instability corridors─that remain hidden in traditional approaches. By reframing reaction dynamics through intrinsic geometry rather than extrinsic coordinates, this work lays the foundation for a unified geometric description of reaction pathways, stability, and spectroscopy.

item.title: Melt-Processed AgNP-LDPE Nanocomposites with Balanced Antimicrobial and Mechanical Performance for Livestock-Farming Applications
item.description:
Abstract
Bacterial contamination in livestock-farming and reproductive-management environments creates a need for antimicrobial polymer materials with reliable processability, mechanical performance, and application-related compatibility. In this study, poly(vinylpyrrolidone) (PVP)-stabilized silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) were synthesized and incorporated into low-density polyethylene (LDPE) using a masterbatch-based melt-processing approach. AgNP formation was confirmed by UV–vis spectroscopy, TEM, and FTIR. The synthesized AgNPs showed antimicrobial activity against bacterial isolates from boar semen and sow vaginal discharge, and time-kill analysis demonstrated time- and dose-dependent bacterial inhibition. A 25 kg AgNP-rich LDPE masterbatch was prepared by industrial-scale extrusion, and diluted to produce the AgNP-LDPE nanocomposites containing 50, 100, and 500 ppm AgNPs. The nanocomposites were evaluated in terms of Ag distribution, mechanical properties, thermal behavior, Ag+ release, antibacterial activity, boar semen quality, and fertility performance in sows. Loadings of 50 and 100 ppm maintained or improved tensile performance, whereas 500 ppm reduced tensile strength and ductility. The 50 and 100 ppm nanocomposites exhibited progressive Ag+ release and strong antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli, Staphylococcus aureus, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The semen tubes containing 50 and 100 ppm AgNPs showed no significant adverse effects on sperm motility, progressive motility, pregnancy rate, or farrowing rate. These results identify 50–100 ppm as an effective loading range for melt-processed AgNP-LDPE nanocomposites with balanced antimicrobial performance, mechanical properties, and application-related compatibility for livestock-farming applications.

item.title: Polyacetylenes from Lobelia chinensis with Dermal Papilla Cell Proliferative Activity and Their Enhanced Production through Elicitation
item.description:
Abstract
Lobelia chinensis is a medicinal plant containing a wide variety of bioactive constituents. In the present study, a 50% methanol extract of L. chinensis significantly promoted the proliferation of human dermal papilla (DP) cells. The n-BuOH fraction was identified as the most active fraction, from which eight compounds were isolated and identified as four polyacetylenes, lobetyolinin (1), lobetyolin (2), pratiallin B (3), and tangshenyne B (4), two lignans, dehydrodiconiferyl alcohol 4-O-β-D-glucopyranoside (5) and urolignoside (6), and two nitrogen-containing compounds, tryptophan (7) and adenosine (8). Six compounds (1–4, 6, and 7) significantly stimulated DP cell proliferation, indicating that polyacetylenes are major contributors to the biological activity of L. chinensis. To enhance the production of the major active polyacetylenes, in vitro shoot cultures were treated with various elicitors. Quantitative HPLC analysis demonstrated elicitor-dependent changes in the accumulation of lobetyolinin (1) and lobetyolin (2), with 100 mg L–1 yeast extract producing the highest levels of both compounds. Extracts from elicitor-treated cultures also exhibited enhanced DP cell proliferative activity compared with untreated cultures, suggesting that the enhanced biological activity is associated with coordinated changes in multiple bioactive constituents rather than with the increased accumulation of a single compound. These findings identify major polyacetylenes contributing to the DP cell proliferative activity of L. chinensis and link their biological activity with elicitor-assisted metabolite production, providing a practical strategy for the sustainable production of standardized L. chinensis materials with potential hair-growth-promoting applications.

item.title: Development of Supramolecular Calix[4]arene-MCM-Based Nanomaterials Doped with CuNPs: An Inorganic–Organic Hybrid Recyclable Nanoenzyme as a Potent Peroxidase and Oxidase Mimic
item.description:
Abstract
An inorganic–organic hybrid nanomaterial, Cu@MCMCal, was synthesized by immobilizing p-tert-butyl calix[4]arene on to mesoporous silica followed by incorporation of CuNPs. The synthesized nanomaterial was characterized extensively using various analytical techniques such as FT-IR, UV–Vis spectroscopy, TEM, PXRD, XPS, Cu LMM Auger, BET, and TGA analyses. The hybrid nanomaterial was evaluated for its catalytic performance toward peroxidase-like activity using 3,3′,5,5′-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) and o-phenylenediamine (OPD) as a substrate at room temperature at pH 4.5 in acetate buffer and pH 7.4 in PBS buffer, respectively. Enzyme kinetics was performed for both the substrates using the Michaelis–Menten steady-state kinetics and the Lineweaver–Burk plot to determine the catalytic affinity. Based on the kinetic measurements, the values of the Km for TMB and OPD were found to be 0.661 ± 0.143 and 0.606 ± 0.061 mM, respectively. The hybrid nanoenzyme also exhibits the oxidase-like activity using dopamine as a substrate at pH 7.4 in PBS buffer. The Cu@MCMCal nanomaterial acted as a nanoenzyme, efficient for catalysis toward oxidation reactions with better cost effectiveness and improved stability and recyclability as compared to biological enzymes. Therefore, a promising, stable, efficient, and robust nanoenzyme has been development for oxidation reactions.

item.title: Resource Analysis and Screening for Potential CO 2 Storage Targets in Low-Porosity Saline Aquifers, Yulin, China
item.description:
Abstract
The Ordos Basin, a crucial energy base in China, leads the nation in oil, gas, and coal production, consequently leading to high carbon emissions. This establishes it as a key prospective region for implementing CO2 geological storage (CCS) to facilitate regional emissions reductions. However, the basin is predominantly characterized by low-porosity and ultralow-permeability reservoirs, which limit the applicability of current site selection criteria, largely derived from successful international projects involving high-porosity and high-permeability reservoirs. There is a lack of systematic site selection research tailored to such low-quality reservoirs. Therefore, this study focuses on screening target areas for the CO2 storage. On the basis of well-logging and geological data from 192 wells in the Yulin area of the Ordos Basin, we systematically conducted lithostratigraphic correlation, reservoir property interpretation, and deep saline aquifer identification. This resulted in the identification of two saline aquifers: the Chang 10-3 Submember of the Yanchang Formation (with an average porosity of 8.3% and a maximum permeability of 12.3 mD) and the Qian 5 Member of the Shiqianfeng Formation (with an average porosity of 8.5% and a maximum permeability of 8.3 mD). We then developed the low-porosity and low-permeability evaluation index system (LOWEIS), a dedicated framework integrating and quantifying more than ten key indicators, including the sand-to-formation ratio, single-layer thickness, porosity, permeability, shale-to-formation ratio, and social environmental constraints. Applying the LOWEIS for hierarchical evaluation and spatial overlay analysis across the 14,000 km2 area of Yulin, China, we preliminarily identified 8 favorable storage targets with the highest implementation potential. This work complements existing site selection techniques for CO2 geological storage and provides a targeted evaluation framework for low-porosity and low-permeability saline aquifers.

item.title: Migration Mechanisms and Spatial Differentiation of Elements in Coal under Stress Action
item.description:
Abstract
Tectonic stress is an important factor that controls elemental migration in coal. However, the mechanisms underlying stress-induced elemental migration and the factors controlling the resulting spatial differentiation remain poorly understood. In this study, high-temperature and high-pressure simulation experiments were employed as the primary approach. By integrating the macroscopic deformation characteristics of coal with the evolution of its molecular structure at the microscopic scale, we investigated the stress-induced migration mechanisms and spatial differentiation characteristics of the elements in coal. The results show that tectonic stress induces compaction and structural reconstruction of the coal, forming an elemental migration pattern driven by stress gradients, and with fractures serving as the principal migration pathways. On the basis of the stress response characteristics and vertical variation rates of elements in coal, three response mechanisms were identified: stress-enrichment, stress-depletion, and stress-insensitive types. The stress-induced migration of elements in coal is governed by the coupled effects of the stress–strain environment and intrinsic physicochemical properties of the elements. Deformation and failure of the coal structure provide important migration channels for elemental transport. Moreover, tectonic stress affects the evolution of coal macromolecular structures through stress degradation, thereby altering elemental binding sites and promoting element migration in coal.

item.title: Predictive Optimization of Vibrations in a Biodiesel-Fueled Variable Compression Ratio Engine Using BO-CNN-LSTM
item.description:
Abstract
Integrating sustainable biodiesel blends into variable compression ratio (VCR) diesel engines significantly alters combustion dynamics and structural vibrations. The present study introduces a Bayesian optimized 1D convolutional neural network-long-short-term memory (CNN-LSTM) deep learning framework designed for optimizing the multiaxis engine vibrations. The predictive architecture processes a six-parameter input matrix encompassing engine load, compression ratio (CR), and critical thermophysical fuel properties. A precise evaluation demonstrated the superior fidelity of the hybrid network, achieving up to a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.985 and a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.288 m/s2, substantially outperforming optimized support vector machine (SVM) and multilayer perceptron (MLP) benchmarks. Multiaxis spatial stability was visually confirmed using Taylor diagrams, while a 3000-iteration bootstrap analysis validated algorithmic robustness within a narrow 95% confidence interval (0.38–0.79 m/s2). Permutation feature importance and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis clarified the thermodynamic decision-making process, revealing that elevated engine load and CR intensify mechanical ringing, whereas the higher density and viscosity of biodiesel blends act as natural vibration dampeners. High-resolution contour maps generated through systematic response surface mapping provided precise predictive optimization surfaces. Deploying this advanced methodology establishes a highly reliable, cost-effective virtual calibration tool for next-generation biodiesel-fueled engines, eliminating the necessity for exhaustive physical testing.

item.title: Trinor-Guaiane-Type Sesquiterpenes with Unusual Skeletons from the Okinawan Soft Coral Clavularia viridis
item.description:
Abstract
Four new trinor-guaiane sesquiterpenes, clavuridin C (1), clavuridin D (2), 5-methoxyclavuridin B (3), and 5-epi-clavuridin B (4), together with three known compounds, clavuridin B (6), clavularin A (7), and clavularin B (8), were isolated from the soft coral Clavularia viridis collected from the coast of Cape Kyan, Okinawa Prefecture, Japan. The structures of the newly isolated compounds 1–4, including their relative configurations, were elucidated through detailed analysis of spectroscopic data, such as IR, NMR, MS, and density functional theory (DFT)-based DP4 analysis, as well as by comparison with previously reported related compounds. The absolute configurations of 2 and 3 were additionally investigated through electronic circular dichroism (ECD) calculations. The absolute configuration of 4 was determined through benzoylation, followed by application of the allylic benzoate rule. Furthermore, structural differences between 4 and antheliol (4a) were addressed through detailed comparison of experimental and calculated NMR data, including DP4 and CP3 analyses, leading to a revision of the previously proposed structure. These results highlight the importance of integrated spectroscopic and computational approaches for accurate structure determination of closely related sesquiterpenes. In addition, isolated compounds 1–4 and 6–8 were evaluated for their antibacterial and antifungal activities.

item.title: Salt Effects on the Growth of Mixed Anionic and Zwitterionic Surfactant Micelles
item.description:
Abstract
We investigate the changes in 3:1 mixed sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) and cocamidopropyl betaine (CAPB) surfactant solutions (at the 400 mM scale) upon addition of alkali/halide salts up to a concentration of 2.5 M using coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations coupled with a Hamiltonian replica exchange scheme and accounting for long-range electrostatic effects. Upon addition of salt, micelle properties (size, morphology, degree of neutralization, equilibrium between surfactant chains within ‘end-cap’ and ‘cylindrical’ micellar subdomains) as well as surfactant solution shear viscosities all obey a linear regime until a salt concentration of about 1 M. Then, they obey a new regime in which they all rapidly and nonlinearly diverge, in line with available experimental evidence regarding similar mixed anionic/zwitterionic surfactant solutions. Interestingly, the transition between these two regimes can be rationalized by considering an equilibrium between only SDS chains in ‘end-cap’ and ‘cylindrical’ micelle domains (according to the pseudophase thermodynamic framework), with CAPB chains taken into account implicitly. Although there is room for improvement, our simulation protocol appears to be a promising tool to investigate the effects of cosurfactants and/or hydrophobic (fragrance) molecules on surfactant solutions.

item.title: Bioinformatics-Driven Identification of Flooding-Tolerance Genes and Their Structural and Molecular Characterization in Soybean
item.description:
Abstract
Flooding stress is one of the important abiotic factors restricting soybean production globally. Despite numerous efforts, the genetic mechanisms of flooding tolerance are not fully understood. This work used a bioinformatics-driven, integrative approach combining structural analysis, molecular docking, expression profiling, and biochemical phenotyping to prioritize and characterize genes associated with flooding tolerance (FTgenes) during the early stages of soybean seedling development. Functional annotation of 83 previously prioritized FTgenes was used to classify them into five functional categories, with one candidate per category identified for further study: enolase (energy supply); phytocyanin (reactive oxygen species; ROS management); glycoside hydrolase family 17 (GH17; cell wall adjustment); ethylene and sulfur compound biosynthesis-related protein (ESCBp; hormonal signaling); and alfin zinc-finger protein (gene regulation). Comprehensive sequence analyses, phylogenetic relationships, motif predictions, and homology modeling were performed for these five candidate genes. Molecular docking analyses demonstrated that enolase, GH17, and ESCBp had conserved residues necessary for catalysis and forming stable complexes with respective ligands. Expression analysis showed distinct but coordinated transcriptional activation of the FTgenes during short-term flooding stress. Levels of salicylic acid and abscisic acid changed as a function of time upon flooding. In addition, protein levels, chlorophyll a content, total phenolics, flavonoids, and antioxidant capacity were modulated in an organ-dependent manner. Overall, this study has provided evidence for a coordinated network of energy metabolism, ROS homeostasis, cell wall adjustment, hormone signaling, and regulation of gene expression that characterizes the early molecular response of soybean seedlings to flooding stress. These genes provide structurally and molecularly characterized candidate genes for future genetic improvement.

item.title: Sequence-Activity Relationships and Integrated In Silico and In Vitro Mechanistic Study of the Antimicrobial Peptide PEP-4 against Staphylococcus aureus
item.description:
Abstract
The rise of antimicrobial resistance among ESKAPE pathogens demands novel therapeutic strategies. Here, we evaluate a panel of five synthetic peptides through integrated in vitro and in silico analyses, highlighting PEP-4 as a promising antibacterial lead peptide. Our findings demonstrate the key role of C-terminal hydrophobic patterning in antimicrobial efficacy. PEP-4 exhibits strong antibacterial activity (MIC 15.6–62.5 μg mL–1, corresponding to ∼10.5–41.9 μM) and consistently shows bactericidal effects against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative strains. Molecular dynamics simulations show sustained, charge-selective interaction of PEP-4 with an anionic S. aureus-like bilayer and only intermittent association with a zwitterionic mammalian model, supporting electrostatically driven membrane recognition as the initial step of its mechanism; no bilayer destabilization was observed in either system over the simulated time scale. Additionally, molecular docking suggests potential secondary intracellular protein targets. Notably, PEP-4 retains activity in the presence of lysyl-phospholipid-mediated resistance in Staphylococcus aureus, yet exhibits only transient interactions with zwitterionic mammalian membranes. This selective membrane binding is consistent with low cytotoxicity to humans, corroborated by other in silico predictions. It suggests a potential therapeutic window, pending experimental validation, supporting PEP-4 as a promising peptide scaffold for next-generation antimicrobial design.

item.title: Numerical Simulation of Spatial Distribution Characteristics of Hazardous Gas Clouds from Leakage at a Hydrogen-Blended Natural Gas Distribution Station
item.description:
Abstract
Blending hydrogen into natural gas pipelines is widely regarded as a promising transitional pathway for large-scale H2 transport; however, it inevitably increases the risk of leaks and explosions at urban distribution stations. This computational fluid dynamics (CFD) study models a typical gas distribution station, employing LFL isosurface area and volume to evaluate the effects of the hydrogen blending ratio (HBR), operating pressure, leakage aperture, wind speed, wind direction, and leak direction on hazardous gas cloud evolution. The results show rapid initial growth in both surface area and volume; the surface area subsequently stabilizes, while the volume continues to rise, indicating continuous hazard zone expansion. A higher HBR broadens the LFL isosurface and promotes a vertical dispersion. Wind speed has a nonlinear influence, while wind direction and leak orientation govern accumulation patterns through the building obstructions. Sensitivity analysis identifies leakage aperture and leak direction as the most influential continuous and categorical factors, respectively, with operating pressure ranking second and HBR and wind speed ranking third. These findings provide support for safety distance determination, leakage aperture monitoring, and emergency response planning for hydrogen-blended gas distribution stations.

item.title: Virtual Screening for Dual Inhibitors of HDAC6 and MPO: A Multistep Approach Integrating Chemical Space Analysis and Molecular Docking
item.description:
Abstract
Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) remain the leading cause of mortality worldwide, accounting for ∼17.9 million deaths annually. Despite therapeutic advances, treatments face limitations, such as adverse effects, drug resistance, and high costs. CVDs involve complex biological networks and compensatory pathways that limit the efficacy of single-targeted therapies. In this context, the multitarget-directed ligand (MTDL) strategy has emerged as a promising approach to enhance therapeutic efficacy by modulating proteins in different biochemical pathways involved in disease progression. Thus, this work reports a virtual screening study aimed at identifying novel dual inhibitors targeting histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6) and myeloperoxidase (MPO), two enzymes implicated in the pathophysiology of CVDs and associated risk factors, for which no multitarget inhibition studies have been reported to date. Both targets converge in exacerbating CVDs by driving vascular inflammation and impairing cardiac autophagy. In this way, a ligand- and structure-based virtual screening approach was employed to identify potential multitarget hit compounds. The selection of reference compounds for virtual screening was based on four strategies combining the lowest IC50 values, clinical status, and shared physicochemical properties between the inhibitors of both enzymes, selected from a chemical space analysis. Molecular similarity was assessed via the Tanimoto index using reference ligands followed by molecular docking. Molecules 11 and 16 emerged as putative dual inhibitors, exhibiting structural similarity and crucial active-site interactions with HDAC6 (Zn2+) and MPO (heme, His95, Arg239). These findings support further investigation of these molecules as potential lead compounds for a dual-target cardiovascular therapy.

item.title: Ionic Liquid-Assisted Synthesis of Ce-Doped NiCo-Based Composite Electrocatalysts for Hydrogen Evolution
item.description:
Abstract
Developing efficient and low-cost electrocatalysts is an urgent need for water splitting. Water splitting relies on a wide range of catalysts. Owing to its flexible coordination chemistry and outstanding redox properties, cerium (Ce) not only functions as an active catalyst on its own but also serves as an effective promoter for other catalytic species. This paper prepared NiCo-PBA based on the “nanoregions” formed in an ionic liquid mixture system, synthesized Ce-doped nickel–cobalt-based Prussian blue analogues through ion exchange reactions, and successfully prepared porous composite materials CeNiCo@NC with different Ce contents by calcination in an inert atmosphere. The research results show that the resulting Ce-doped NiCo@NC materials with rationally optimized Ce contents deliver remarkable HER activity, making them promising candidates as efficient water-splitting catalysts. In particular, CeNiCo@NC-3 exhibits the highest electrocatalytic performance among the series, delivering 10 mA cm–2 at only 99 mV overpotential, 57 mV (36.5%) lower than that of Ce-free NiCo@NC-500. Additionally, its Tafel slope of 61 mV dec–1 corresponds to a 15.3% improvement over NiCo@NC-500. The origin of this enhanced activity lies in the enlarged electrochemically active surface area, expedited charge transfer, and the promotion of Ce3+ ↔ Ce4+ conversion in CeO2 after the introduction of Ce.

item.title: PDA-Assisted Fabrication of Calcium Alginate Hydrogel-Coated Stainless Steel Meshes for High-Efficiency Oil/Water Separation
item.description:
Abstract
This study introduces an environmentally friendly and straightforward dip-coating technique for preparing stainless steel meshes (SSM) coated with calcium alginate (CA) hydrogel. The prepared mesh possesses high hydrophilicity and underwater superoleophobicity, enabling highly efficient separation of diverse oil/water mixtures. Initially, dopamine undergoes in situ self-polymerization to form a polydopamine (PDA) interlayer anchored on the SSM substrate. This PDA layer was then firmly coated with sodium alginate (SA) through hydrogen bonding and electrostatic interactions. The introduction of Ca2+ facilitates the formation of a stable CA composite hydrogel coating on the substrate surface via metal-ion coordination and chelation. Characterization results demonstrated that the CA hydrogel introduced abundant hydrophilic functional groups and micro/nanoscale hierarchical roughness on the mesh surface, significantly enhancing its wettability. The treated mesh exhibited underwater–oil contact angles (UOCA) greater than 153° for various oils, accompanied by an in-air water contact angle (WCA) of 18.3°. It also demonstrates superior antifouling properties and recyclability. Utilizing only gravitational force, the coated mesh demonstrated effective separation of multiple oil/water mixtures. The separation efficiency consistently exceeds 99%, achieving a maximum water flux of 31254 L·m–2·h–1. Remarkably, the mesh’s separation ability was not impaired by exposure to harsh stimuli, including UV exposure, various corrosive solutions, mechanical damage, and extreme thermal cycling, demonstrating its high environmental adaptability. Given its environmentally friendly preparation method and superior properties, this coated mesh shows great promise for practical applications in treating oily wastewater and addressing challenges associated with aquatic environment remediation.

item.title: Structure-Guided Optimization of a LipL32-Targeting DNA Aptamer through Molecular Dynamics and Free-Energy Analysis
item.description:
Abstract
Accurate detection of leptospirosis requires high-affinity recognition of the conserved LipL32 biomarker. Although LipL32-targeting DNA aptamers have been identified through systematic evolution of ligands by exponential enrichment (SELEX), the molecular basis of their target recognition remains unclear, limiting rational post-SELEX optimization. Here, we investigated the molecular recognition mechanism of the LepDapt-5 aptamer family using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and binding free-energy analysis. We generated three-dimensional aptamer models using AlphaFold 3 (AF3) and constructed protein–aptamer docking complexes with HADDOCK, showing a stable G-quadruplex (GQ) motif within the aptamer core. Structural and energetic analyses identified key domains contributing to LipL32 binding, while per-residue energy decomposition highlighted nucleotides suitable for rational sequence refinement. Guided by these insights, we introduced targeted single-point mutations, evaluated their effects computationally, and validated their performance experimentally using enzyme-linked aptamer sorbent assays (ELASA). Relative binding free energies (ΔΔGbind) calculated using nonequilibrium alchemical MD showed strong agreement with ELASA measurements: T19A reduced binding affinity, G7C produced minimal change, and G24C significantly enhanced affinity. Experimental equilibrium dissociation constants (KD) further supported these predictions, identifying G24C as the highest-affinity variant. Additionally, the G24C mutant retained strong binding to LipL32 while exhibiting no detectable binding to the NS1 protein of dengue virus 2 and the E2 protein of Chikungunya virus.

item.title: Thermally Tuned Acceleration of Photoinduced Crawling Motion in Azobenzene Crystals and Enhanced Particle Transport
item.description:
Abstract
Mechanically responsive organic crystals are attracting increasing attention as soft actuators. However, precise control over the velocity of their continuous translational motion remains a challenge. Crystals of trans-3,3′-dimethylazobenzene (DMAB) exhibit continuous crawling motion on solid surfaces under simultaneous irradiation with ultraviolet (UV) and visible light from opposite directions. In this study, we controlled the velocity of photoinduced crawling motion in DMAB crystals through temperature modulation. A 5 °C increase in substrate temperature markedly changed the crawling velocity. Within the investigated temperature range, the maximum velocity at 30 °C reached 13.4 ± 4.4 μm min–1, more than three times the velocity at 25 °C (4.2 ± 1.7 μm min–1). In contrast, at 35 °C, crawling motion was barely observed, and the maximum velocity decreased significantly to 4.7 ± 3.2 μm min–1. Polarized optical microscopy and microspectroscopy provided insights into the temperature-dependent crawling mechanism by revealing the dynamics of melting and recrystallization under UV and visible light irradiation. Furthermore, the rapid crawling motion at 30 °C was maintained during silica microparticle transport, improving the transport step in cargo capture–carry–release tasks based on the photoinduced crawling motion of DMAB crystals. This represents a notable improvement over previous studies, which did not achieve comparable acceleration of the motion.

item.title: Deep Learning for Protein Secondary-Structure Segmentation in Intermediate-Resolution Cryo-EM Maps: A Resolution-Stratified Benchmark Dataset and Controlled Evaluation
item.description:
Abstract
Accurate segmentation of protein secondary structures in cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) maps is crucial for protein tracing and atomic model building, yet remains challenging at intermediate resolutions. Although deep learning architectures have recently been applied to this task, there remains a lack of standardized evaluation protocols and systematic resolution-stratified analyses. Consequently, it remains unclear how segmentation performance varies across finer resolution ranges within the intermediate-resolution regime and how different volumetric segmentation architectures compare under controlled experimental conditions. To address these gaps, we present a nonredundant, resolution-stratified benchmark dataset and a controlled evaluation framework for protein secondary-structure segmentation in intermediate-resolution cryo-EM maps. The dataset comprises 972 nonredundant protein-chain samples from 495 cryo-EM protein structures resolved at 4.5–8.0 Å, with voxel-level annotations for helices, sheets, and non-periodic secondary-structure (NPSS) regions. The dataset is stratified into three resolution ranges─4.5–5.5, 5.5–6.5, and 6.5–8.0 Å─to enable systematic analysis of resolution-dependent segmentation performance. Using this benchmark, we evaluate five representative convolutional and transformer-based volumetric segmentation architectures─U-Net, Residual U-Net, Attention U-Net, UNETR, and Swin-UNETR─under standardized preprocessing, training, and evaluation protocols. Residual U-Net achieves the highest macro-averaged foreground (Macro-FG) F1 score in all three resolution bins, while helices are segmented more accurately than sheets and NPSS regions. All five architectures achieve their highest Macro-FG F1 scores in the highest-resolution bin, whereas performance varies between the two lower-resolution bins across architectures and secondary-structure classes. Overall, this benchmark enables fine-grained analysis of resolution-dependent segmentation performance, supports reproducible method development, and facilitates controlled comparison of future cryo-EM secondary-structure segmentation approaches.

item.title: Direct Laser-Heated Pedestal (Czochralski) Growth of Rare-Earth Zirconate A 2 Zr 2 O 7 Single Crystals from Mixed-Oxide Precursors
item.description:
Abstract
High-quality single crystals of refractory oxides are essential for fundamental investigations and advanced functional characterization, yet their preparation is frequently limited by demanding precursor processing and the extremely high temperatures required for crystal growth. Here, we present a practical, reproducible, and experimentally accessible protocol for the preparation of rare-earth zirconate A2Zr2O7 single crystals based on direct processing of mixed-oxide precursors using a laser-heated pedestal (modified Czochralski) technique. In contrast to conventional approaches employing fully reacted polycrystalline feed rods, the proposed route starts directly from homogenized stoichiometric oxide mixtures, substantially simplifying precursor preparation, therefore reducing processing time, energy consumption, handling steps, and opportunities for contamination. The manuscript focuses on the technological aspects of the preparation procedure, including precursor fabrication, optimization of crystal-growth parameters, processing considerations, as well as practical limitations, scope, and applicability of the method. The protocol was successfully applied to 11 selected A2Zr2O7 compositions (A = Y, La, Nd, Eu, Gd, Dy, Ho, Er, Tm, Yb, and Lu), producing centimeter-scale single-crystalline ingots suitable for subsequent materials research. Representative structural and microstructural characterization confirms phase purity, crystallinity, and near-nominal cation stoichiometry, while detailed structural properties of the individual compounds are reported elsewhere. The presented methodology provides a robust and experimentally accessible route for the preparation of high-melting oxide single crystals and may be readily transferable to other refractory oxide systems requiring localized high-temperature melt growth.

item.title: Enhancing the Valorization of Heavy Coal Tar through SBS Modification: Pyrolysis Kinetics and Thermal Conversion Behavior
item.description:
Abstract
Heavy coal tar (HCT), a byproduct of coal pyrolysis, presents challenges in resource utilization due to its complex composition but also provides opportunities for value-added conversion. This study explored the modification of HCT using different SBS copolymers as screening candidates, followed by detailed investigation of a representative SBS-modified system. The structural evolution associated with SBS incorporation was characterized using Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), ultimate analysis, gel permeation chromatography (GPC), and nuclear magnetic resonance (13C NMR). Kinetic analysis and thermodynamic simulation during heat treatment were performed to evaluate the reaction behavior of SBS-modified HCT. The results showed that (1) SBS incorporation did not significantly alter hydroxyl or aliphatic structures in HCT. (2) The normalized elemental composition of MHCT-YH802–4% was represented as C7H8.50N0.04O0.41, and a representative statistical composition of C8.78H10.65N0.05O0.51 was estimated using the GPC-derived Mn. (3) Among the evaluated kinetic models, the three-dimensional diffusion function showed a relatively better fit under the investigated heating conditions and was therefore selected as an empirical mathematical descriptor of the overall thermal conversion behavior. These results underscore the potential of polymer-modified HCT in providing a basis for precursor structure control and thermal behavior analysis.

item.title: Evaluation of Attalea tessmannii Kernel Oil as a Feedstock for Biodiesel Production by Methanolysis and Ethanolysis
item.description:
Abstract
Biodiesel production has been investigated due to its potential to mitigate pollutant gas emissions through the partial replacement of petroleum diesel. Although the technology is well-established, continued research focuses on the evaluation of alternative feedstocks and production routes that improve performance and economic viability. In this study, oil extracted from the kernels of Attalea tessmannii, a highly saturated oil obtained from an Amazonian fruit, was assessed as a feedstock for biodiesel production via methanolysis and ethanolysis. Crude and neutralized oils were subjected to base-catalyzed transesterification, and the resulting biofuels were characterized in terms of ester content, density, kinematic viscosity, acidity index, thermal behavior, and flash point. Oil refining resulted in an overall yield of 87%, while transesterification achieved ester contents of up to 93% for methanolysis and 97% for ethanolysis. The methanolysis products did not meet the minimum ester-content requirement specified by EN 14214 for FAME and also exhibited kinematic viscosities below the EN 14214 range. In contrast, the product obtained by ethanolysis of neutralized oil showed the most favorable overall fuel-quality profile among the evaluated routes, with density of approximately 863 kg m–3, kinematic viscosity near 3.1 mm2 s–1, acidity index below 0.5 mg KOH g–1, and flash point of 139 °C. A preliminary economic assessment revealed raw-material costs ranging from 0.536 to 0.712 USD kg–1. Although the crude oil–ethanol route presented the lowest production cost and the highest contribution margin per hour, the product obtained from this route exceeded the maximum acid-value limit considered in this study. These findings provide the first experimental evidence that Attalea tessmannii kernel oil is technically compatible with conventional base-catalyzed transesterification, with ethanolysis of neutralized oil offering the most favorable route among those evaluated.

item.title: SizeResGraph-Guided GFN2-xTB Screening of Low-Gap Thiophene-Containing Polymer Repeat Units
item.description:
Abstract
Low-gap conjugated polymers are widely studied for optoelectronic applications, but their vast repeat-unit space makes exhaustive quantum-chemical screening impractical. We developed SizeResGraph, a directed-bond graph neural network with a bounded size-dependent readout, to rank thiophene-containing repeat units by their hydrogen-capped GFN2-xTB HOMO–LUMO gaps. The model learned from 9,905 labeled structures curated from 540,650 public records. Across 10 scaffold partitions and five training seeds, SizeResGraph matched Chemprop D-MPNN within a prespecified ±0.010 eV RMSE equivalence margin. An end-to-end run ranked 419,564 prospective structures in 500.9 s using one RTX 4090 and 16 CPU threads. Direct GFN2-xTB calculations confirmed strong enrichment of the low-gap tail, with Low 5% hit fractions of 88.6% for SizeResGraph and 81.8% for equal-budget Chemprop. In a prediction-independent systematic sample, SizeResGraph predictions showed strong rank agreement with B3LYP-D4/def2-SVP gaps (ρ = 0.836). SizeResGraph combined with targeted quantum-chemical verification therefore provides a scalable route from large repeat-unit libraries to tractable sets of low-gap candidates.

item.title: Rapid Identification of H3N2 Influenza A Virus HA-Targeting Antibody Epitopes Driven by Computational Antibody Similarity Measures
item.description:
Abstract
Antibodies are important therapeutic agents for the prevention and treatment of influenza, and hemagglutinin (HA) serves as the primary target for the development of therapeutic antibodies. However, the identification of epitopes remains an unmet need in the development of such therapeutic antibodies. This study investigates the characteristics of antibody–HA binding interfaces (i.e., epitopes and paratopes) through a computational analysis of all antibody–HA complexes with nonredundant experimentally determined structures from SAbDab, the largest reported antibody structure data set to date. After experimentally identifying and selecting H3N2 HA-specific binding antibodies, a reference antibody library was established. For anti-H3N2 HA antibodies with unknown structures, epitope grouping was conducted based on competitive binding assays that assess interference with the binding of antibodies from the reference library. Based on the complementary relationship between epitope and paratope structures, we selected the structure-based similarity measure most relevant to epitope convergence. Furthermore, we prioritized the experimental validation of binding interference between candidate antibodies and their most structurally similar reference antibodies. We present an integrated computational and experimental framework. This approach includes the construction of an H3N2-specific reference antibody set, computational modeling of antibodies, measurement of antibody similarity, and is complemented by antibody competition binding assays. The dry–wet iterative protocol presented here yielded accurate assessment of the neutralizing potency and breadth of the previously uncharacterized antibody P2A10. Together, the presented pipeline offers a powerful approach for identifying epitopes on anti-H3N2 HA antibodies and for epitope-targeted antibody discovery, while demonstrating the effectiveness of structural analytics in reducing experimental labor.

item.title: Quasi-Ballistic Thermal Transport in Vertically Aligned h-BN
item.description:
Abstract
Hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) has attracted significant interest in the semiconductor industry due to its wide bandgap (5.95 eV), high anisotropic thermal conductivity, and low dielectric constant. However, the formation of crystalline h-BN conventionally requires high processing temperatures, which are incompatible with back-end-of-line (BEOL) integration and advanced packaging processes that must remain below 400 °C to avoid degradation of front-end devices. In this work, trichloroborazine (TCB) was systematically investigated using ammonia as the nitrogen co-reactant under both plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PEALD) and atomic layer annealing (ALA) conditions. In the ALA process, low-energy inert ions are shown to enable in situ crystallization at temperatures well below those required for conventional MOCVD. As a result, highly ordered, vertically aligned polycrystalline h-BN films were deposited within a BEOL-compatible temperature window of 300–400 °C. The as-deposited ALA h-BN films exhibited clear signatures of cross-plane quasi-ballistic phonon transport over a thickness range of 20–50 nm, characterized by a thickness-independent effective thermal resistance of ∼6–9 m2 K GW–1. This invariance with film thickness indicates that phonon mean free paths exceed the film thickness, confirming quasi-ballistic heat transport enabled by the high crystallinity and preferential vertical alignment of the h-BN domains.

item.title: Pu-Doping-Induced Weberite-like Local Motifs and Enhanced Immobilization in Gd 2 Zr 2 O 7 Pyrochlore: A DFT + U Study
item.description:
Abstract
This study employs density functional theory with the Hubbard U correction (DFT + U) method to investigate how Pu incorporation into distinct sites (Gd or Zr) in Gd2Zr2O7 governs locally weberite-like disorder and subsequently influences Pu immobilization behavior. We reveal that incorporating Pu into Zr sites induces spontaneous 48f oxygen displacement toward vacant 8a sites, forming weberite-like local motifs characterized by 7-fold coordinated Pu. This structural disorder increases the oxygen positional parameter xO48f and elongates average Pu–O48f bonds. Solution energies confirm preferential Pu immobilization at Zr sites, where the locally disordered weberite-like arrangement provides additional stabilization. Electronic structure analysis reveals that Pu incorporation into Zr sites induces stronger Pu–O hybridization than Gd-site substitution. Crucially, the 7-coordinated Pu in locally disordered weberite-like arrangements exhibits pronounced ionic character, which could favor Pu immobilization at Zr sites in Gd2Zr2O7. These results suggest that local weberite-like disorder may be a key mechanism for optimizing Pu immobilization in pyrochlore ceramics.

item.title: 3D-Printed GelMA Microneedles with Multilayer Therapeutic Properties for Diabetic Wound-Relevant Drug Delivery
item.description:
Abstract
Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a chronic disease characterized by impaired insulin secretion, reduced insulin sensitivity, and hyperglycemia. Diabetic wounds are among the major complications of T2DM and can lead to chronic wounds due to challenges in the normal healing process. In this study, a three-layered tissue scaffold incorporating microneedles (MNs) was developed for diabetic wound management. The scaffold was fabricated using digital light processing (DLP) for the GelMA-based layers and electrohydrodynamic atomization (EHDA) for the surface coating, combining antibacterial, metabolic, and antioxidant functions within a single platform. The first two layers were designed using gelatin methacrylate (GelMA) and produced via DLP. The first layer was loaded with the antibiotic amoxicillin to prevent infection at the scaffold application site. In the second layer, MNs containing metformin were designed. For the outermost layer, polylactic acid (PLA) microparticles containing antioxidant and antibacterial salicylic acid (SA) were produced via the EHDA method and coated onto the scaffold surface. This three-layered scaffold was characterized by SEM, FT-IR, DSC, and mechanical, swelling, degradation, and penetration analyses. In vitro studies of single-drug-loaded model formulations demonstrated biphasic drug-release behavior over 72 h, effective antibacterial activity against E. coli and S. aureus, and favorable cytocompatibility. Oxidative-stress assays showed lower Total Oxidant Status (TOS) levels and higher Total Antioxidant Status (TAS) values in the drug-loaded formulations, while the scratch assay demonstrated increased wound-gap closure under hyperglycemic culture conditions. Overall, the multilayer microneedle platform exhibited antibacterial activity, with inhibition zones of up to 23 mm, and favorable cytocompatibility, with cell viability remaining above 77% across all formulations. These findings provide in vitro proof-of-concept evidence for the multifunctional design of the platform but do not demonstrate wound-healing efficacy in diabetic tissue.

item.title: Nanoimaging, Spectroscopy, and Biosensor Assays for Alternatively Spliced RNA Isoforms in Disease Diagnostics
item.description:
Abstract
Alternative splicing (AS) generates distinct mRNA isoforms, and frequently distinct proteins, from single genes; its dysregulation is established in cancer, neurodegeneration, and immune disease. Sequencing now nominates candidate splice events at scale, but a nominated event does not become a usable measurement until an isoform-discriminating sequence has been converted into a physical signal. Existing AS reviews concentrate on sequencing workflows, computational event calling, or disease catalogs; the assay-engineering step that follows target nomination remains comparatively underserved, and it is where most translational failures occur. This review addresses that gap. We group postsequencing detection into five classes defined by the physical origin of the signal: (i) fixed-tissue in situ localization, (ii) live-cell RNA imaging, (iii) plasmonic and spectroscopic readouts, (iv) label-free nanophotonic biosensing combined with site-specific RNA processing, and (v) protein-level proteogenomic confirmation. These classes are compared on target definition, reported analytical performance, multiplexing, matrix compatibility, perturbation risk, and clinical readiness. The reported performance spans single-copy imaging of splice variants in living cells to label-free detection at 580 fM in under 30 min without cDNA synthesis or PCR. Three conclusions follow. First, assay selection should be governed by the class of claim being made rather than by platform novelty. Second, analytical sensitivity measured on synthetic targets systematically overstates readiness in clinical matrices; therefore, matrix-matched validation is not optional. Third, cross-laboratory comparison is currently obstructed by inconsistent reporting, which we address by proposing a minimum performance-reporting set and explicit platform-selection criteria. We close with emerging directions, including CRISPR-based isoform detection, biosensor integration with nanopore sequencing, AI-assisted probe design, and digital and microfluidic formats.

item.title: Steric Scaling of Hydrogen Transport in FCC Transition Metals for Mechanically Consistent Molecular Dynamics Simulations
item.description:
Abstract
Hydrogen diffusion in face-centered cubic metals is examined using replicate-resolved molecular dynamics that quantifies temperature-dependent transport and lattice stability. Transport in Ni, Co and Pd is modeled with a hybrid embedded-atom method/Lennard-Jones framework at 800, 900, 1000, and 1250 K. Rather than fitting hydrogen–metal interactions to a single diffusivity, migration energetics are constrained through steric scaling of the FCC interstitial geometry. All baseline finite-concentration parametrizations remain structurally stable under the monitored lattice-volume criteria. Volume fluctuations stay below 0.15% and swelling below 0.09%. Late-time mean-squared displacement remains linear in all accepted trajectories. Four-temperature Arrhenius fits are stable for Ni, Co, and uniform Pd, while scaled Pd remains less constrained. The expected diffusivity hierarchy DPd > DCo ≈ DNi is recovered. Steric scaling lowers Pd diffusivity at every temperature while leaving Ni and Co unchanged, since their interaction parameters are fixed. Pathway-resolved single-H calculations give 0 K barriers of 0.1516 eV for Ni and 0.1294 eV for Co. For Pd, scaling raises the verified static barrier from 0.0234 to 0.0398 eV. A higher-loading Pd test retains the diffusivity reduction while lattice swelling remains bounded. Steric scaling therefore modulates the resolved migration landscape while preserving lattice stability and the observed finite-temperature diffusivity trends.

item.title: Dual-Kinetic Relaxation Spectroscopy for Discrimination of Volatile Organic Mixtures via Finite-Size Surface Gratings
item.description:
Abstract
Discrimination of chemically similar volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in gas mixtures remains a challenge for traditional optical refractive index sensors. In this work, we used a surface holographic grating relaxation technique to monitor the transport kinetics of VOCs. By analyzing the decay of the diffraction efficiency, we extract two independent relaxation time constants. These constants arise from the interplay between the local diffusion of the gas molecules through the material and the geometric aperture losses of the sensing surface (diffusion of molecules in air underneath the grating sensor). These parameters provide a unique kinetic fingerprint for individual species. Mapping these values in a 2D inverse-time state space reveals distinct, nonoverlapping clusters. Furthermore, in the presence of multicomponent gas molecules, by mapping the relaxation lifetimes of pure volatiles and their binary mixtures, we identify a predictable transition in the state space. This approach enables the discrimination between individual volatile compounds and mixtures (e.g., methanol-ethanol) and, in principle, allows their respective concentrations to be quantified and monitored over time with a high degree of sensitivity. This dual-parameter approach uses the finite-size effects of the probe beam, traditionally considered an experimental limitation, to enhance sensor selectivity, offering a robust framework for miniaturizing complex gas-phase analysis.

item.title: Quantification of Partial Oxidation of Magnetite to Maghemite in Aqueous Solution Using XRD
item.description:
Abstract
In aqueous solutions, magnetite (Fe3O4) nanoparticles (NPs) easily oxidize into a material with crystalline characteristics in between magnetite and maghemite (γ-Fe2O3), inevitably modifying their properties. The routine quantification and characterization of this transformation were previously hampered by the structural similarity of magnetite and maghemite. Here, we compared X-ray Absorption Fine Structure (XAFS) characterization to laboratory-based X-ray Diffraction (XRD) pattern analysis, such as Rietveld refinement and peak position shifts of the (311), (400), (511), and (440) reflections, to determine if XRD can be used to determine magnetite oxidation by itself. We analyzed the transformation extent of nanoparticles (10 nm) reacting under different concentrations of oxidizing agents such as O2 and H2O2. We showed that XRD methods─Rietveld refinements and single peak, such as (511)-based─can within error reproduce XAFS results. Our results document a more accessible characterization method for the quantification of magnetite NPs partial oxidation in solution.

item.title: Waterborne Hydrophobic Hard Coatings Based on Fluorinated Silica with Maintained Optical Transparency for Automotive Display Films
item.description:
Abstract
A waterborne fluorinated silica nanoemulsion was developed as a multifunctional additive for transparent automotive display coatings. Aqueous colloidal silica was first functionalized with γ-methacryloxypropyltrimethoxysilane (γ-MPS), followed by KPS-initiated polymerization of dodecafluoroheptyl methacrylate (DFMA). The modified silica was blended with a waterborne acrylate emulsion and wet-coated onto PC/PMMA films. Solid-state 29Si NMR confirmed γ-MPS condensation through the formation of T2 and T3 species, while XPS verified the introduction of DFMA-derived fluorinated groups. The optimized coating exhibited a water contact angle of approximately 107°, pencil hardness up to 3H, and visible-light transmittance of about 90% or higher. Fingerprint contamination and wiping tests further demonstrated improved easy-clean performance; the haze of the coated film decreased to approximately 0.99% after only two wiping steps, compared with 1.52% for bare PC/PMMA under the same conditions. After 100 steel-wool abrasion cycles, the transmittance change was limited to 0.4%, compared with 0.9% for the unfilled acrylic coating and 2.7% for bare PC/PMMA. SEM analysis confirmed reduced scratching and surface deformation. These results demonstrate a promising waterborne route to transparent, hydrophobic, easy-clean, and abrasion-resistant coatings for automotive display applications.

item.title: Presowing Management as a Factor Influencing Vegetative, Reproductive, and Biochemical Performance in Soybean Seed Production
item.description:
Abstract
Although chemical, biological, and vitamin-based seed treatments are individually well documented in soybean, comparative evidence on their combined application within a single experimental framework remains scarce. This study evaluated the effects of treating soybean seeds with a chemical product, Azospirillum spp. (2 mL kg–1 of seed), and the B-complex vitamins pyridoxine (B6) and nicotinamide (B3) (100 mg kg–1 of seed), applied alone and in combination, on gas exchange, vegetative growth, reproductive performance, and seed biochemical composition of soybean grown under greenhouse conditions. Seed treatments altered intercellular CO2 concentration and increased carboxylation efficiency, without significantly affecting net photosynthesis, stomatal conductance, transpiration, or water use efficiency. Treated plants showed greater plant height, branching, and pod number, together with higher seed number and mass, with Azospirillum spp producing the most consistent gains. Protein, lipid, amino acid, and soluble sugar contents increased with seed treatment, while proline remained unchanged, indicating a beneficial physiological stimulus rather than a stress response. These findings show that combining chemical, biological, and vitamin-based seed treatments improves vigor and early performance in soybean seed production and provide a practical basis for developing multi-input seed treatment protocols, although validation under field conditions is still required.

item.title: Optimization and Application of ReaxFF for the Aqueous Carbonation of Calcium Silicates in Steel Slag
item.description:
Abstract
The existing ReaxFF for the C/H/O/Ca/Si system exhibits poor compatibility with aqueous multiphase reactions. In this work, the aqueous carbonation of dicalcium silicate (C2S) derived from steel slag was selected as the research system, and parameter optimization and validation of the reactive force field were performed. Density functional theory with the GGA-PBE functional was adopted to conduct structural relaxation and potential energy surface scanning for C2S polymorphs, carbonate species, and reaction intermediates, and a comprehensive structure-energy training data set was established. Subsequently, ReaxFF parameters were trained using the ParAMS module, and molecular dynamics simulations of aqueous C2S carbonation were implemented via the LAMMPS code. The results show that the equation-of-state curves (volume-energy, bond length-energy, etc.) of the optimized C/H/O/Ca/Si force field agree well with the DFT reference data, which effectively addresses the difficulty in characterizing multiphase interfacial reactions involving water molecules. This optimized force field was applied to 10 ns MD simulations for the aqueous carbonation of β-C2S and γ-C2S. The simulations successfully reproduced the efficient adsorption and accumulation of CO2 and H2O on the C2S surface, while maintaining favorable computational efficiency with conventional computing resources. The force field parameters obtained in this study provide a robust computational tool for further elucidating the microscopic mechanism of aqueous carbon sequestration by calcium silicates.

item.title: Structure–Property Relationships of PAM/CMC-Based Semi-IPN Hydrogels: Influence of APS/ANI Ratio on Swelling, Electrical, Thermal, and Morphological Properties
item.description:
Abstract
In this work, semi-interpenetrating network (semi-IPN) hydrogels based on polyacrylamide (PAM)/CMC matrices incorporating polyaniline (PANI) were synthesized to investigate the influence of the ammonium persulfate/aniline (APS/ANI) ratio on structure–property relationships. Hydrogels were prepared via free radical polymerization of PAM/CMC followed by in situ polymerization of aniline within the preformed matrix, yielding composites with systematically varied APS/ANI ratios. Swelling studies in 1.0 mol L–1 HCl revealed that the incorporation of PANI reduced the equilibrium electrolyte swelling degree relative to PAM/CMC hydrogels, yet promoted specific ionic interactions with Cl– ions, strongly dependent on the oxidant/monomer ratio. Electrical conductivity analysis reached values up to 10–2 S·cm–1, with the highest performance observed for hydrogels synthesized at intermediate APS/ANI ratios. Morphological (SEM/EDX) and structural (FTIR, UV–Vis, XRD) analyses demonstrated that PANI formed dendritic-like microstructures distributed within the CMC-containing matrix, while XRD results correlated crystallinity variations with electrical performance. Thermal analysis (TGA) indicated differences in the thermal degradation behavior of the composites compared with the PAM/CMC matrix. These findings highlight the central role of the APS/ANI ratio in modulating the swelling, structural organization, and electroactive properties of PAM/CMC/PANI semi-IPN hydrogels, providing insights for the design of polysaccharide-based conductive materials with potential applications in electroactive devices.

item.title: Genetically Expanded Fluorescent SSB T7 RNA Polymerase in Action: Intriguing Photophysics with Enhanced RNA Production
item.description:
Abstract
T7 RNA polymerase (T7-RNAP) is a highly efficient transcriptional enzyme. However, it is prone to mutation at the functionally important Y571 residue, which strongly influences its functional properties. Here, we demonstrate a strategy to modulate the T7-RNAP enzyme by replacing the Y571 residue with a fluorescent triazolyl unnatural amino acid (FTUAA), TCNBAlaAc, via genetic code expansion (GCE) technology using two orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs. Thus, TCNBAlaAc-encoded variants, herein termed SSBT7-RNAP, were successfully expressed, purified, and characterized by SDS-PAGE, MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry, CD, UV–vis, and fluorescence spectroscopy. Incorporation of TCNBAlaAc introduced distinct and enhanced fluorescence signatures while largely preserving the overall secondary structures of the engineered enzymes. Notably, these novel TCNBAlaAc-encoded variants exhibited higher relative RNA yields than those of wild-type T7-RNAP under identical in vitro transcription conditions. Molecular docking further supported the structural compatibility of the modification with the promoter-bound enzyme. These findings establish GCE-based, site-specific incorporation of an FTUAA into a functionally relevant site of T7 RNA polymerase as a promising strategy for generating spectroscopically traceable, transcriptionally competent T7-RNAP variants for future enzyme engineering and mechanistic studies.

item.title: Temperature-Dependent Localized Surface Plasmon Resonance in Gallium Nanoparticles
item.description:
Abstract
The plasmonic characteristics of gallium nanoparticles of varying sizes were explored, with a particular focus on a novel nanometallic form of gallium. We investigate the temperature-dependent plasmonic response of these particles, revealing a unique behavior: gallium nanoparticles lose their plasmonic resonance upon heating and cooling. This reversible plasmonic modulation is accompanied by notable phase stability across a wide temperature range and resistance to ambient air exposure. Our findings highlight the spectral tunability and robustness of gallium-based plasmonic systems, suggesting their strong potential for integration into next-generation nanoscale devices and applications, where dynamic thermal control is advantageous.

item.title: Intramolecular Long-Range Photoinduced Electron Transfer Using π-Way of a Step-π-Conjugated Polymer
item.description:
Abstract
Photoinduced electron transfer (PET) along a π-scaffold with breaks remains poorly understood. To address this, we showed that a step-π-conjugated polymer (SPP)─made of alternating pyrrole rings and a single sp3 carbon─enables fast PET through its backbone. In this system, fluorescence quenching occurred when a perylene (Pe) donor was photoexcited in the presence of an anthraquinone (AQ) acceptor. To clarify the quenching mechanism, we considered four possibilities: (i) long-range (pseudo) through-bond PET, (ii) intermolecular through-space PET, (iii) short-range PET (through-space and through-bond), and (iv) intramolecular through-space PET. To systematically test which process dominated, we synthesized three polymers: water-soluble SPP, amphiphilic SPP, and poly(methacrylic acid) sodium salt (PMANa), which lacks π-conjugation. The fluorescence data of these polymers indicate that long-range (pseudo) through-bond PET is the main mechanism in the SPP system. Moreover, femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy reveals a Pe radical cation (Pe•+) and AQ radical anion (AQ•–), confirming charge separation through the step-π-conjugated backbone. The PET (kET) and charge recombination (kCR) rate constants for RDA ≈ 1.8 nm are estimated to be kET > 2 × 1012 s–1 and kCR ≈ 1011 s–1 order, respectively. Thus, SPP enables long-range, fast PFT via a new π-way mechanism.

item.title: Multifunctional CNF-Based Composite with Photochromic and Upconversion Luminescence Properties for Advanced Anticounterfeiting Applications
item.description:
Abstract
The development of advanced security materials with multimodal optical responses is of increasing relevance for anticounterfeiting technologies. In this study, we report the successful synthesis and comprehensive characterization of a multifunctional composite based on cellulose nanofibrils (CNFs) covalently functionalized with photochromic PSPA oligomers and cross-linked with upconversion nanoparticles (UCNPs). Covalent grafting of PSPA onto the CNF backbone was done via Cu0-mediated radical polymerization (SET-LRP) and confirmed by spectroscopic analyses, while microscopic and structural investigations verified the homogeneous incorporation of UCNPs within the nanofibril-based hybrid gel. The resulting material combines reversible photochromic behavior under ultraviolet irradiation with near-infrared (NIR)-to-visible upconversion luminescence, enabling dual-mode optical signaling. The nanocomposite exhibited distinct and reproducible color changes upon UV exposure and characteristic luminescent emission under NIR excitation, demonstrating its suitability for advanced anticounterfeiting applications. Furthermore, the formulation as a stable, printable gel underscores its practical processability and compatibility with scalable anticounterfeiting technologies. The integration of photochromic and upconversion optical functionalities within a renewable CNF-based platform provides a robust, versatile, and sustainable approach for secure labeling and product authentication.

item.title: Optimizing Extraction of Bioactive Compounds from Grape Pomace to Produce an Eco-Friendly Smart Straw
item.description:
Abstract
Grape pomace (GP) is a byproduct rich in bioactive compounds. This study optimized the extraction of these compounds using a Central Composite Rotational Design (CCRD 22), evaluating temperature (41–69 °C) and time (0.8–3.2 h). The optimized extract (GPE) showed high phenolic content (163.99 mg GAE/L), anthocyanins (136.46 mg C3GE/L), and antioxidant activity (69.21% DPPH). GPE was incorporated into babassu mesocarp starch (BS) films, producing an active smart film (GPE-BS) that changed color at extreme pH (2 and 13). The GPE-BS film also showed improved hydrophobicity, antioxidant activity, and elongation at break compared to BS films (control). When tested as a straw for sugar-free cola, the film maintained structural integrity for 2 h. Thus, GPE-BS films are promising for smart food packaging or as edible straws.

item.title: Study on the Photothermal Performance Enhancement of Direct Absorption Solar Collectors by Heat-Transfer-Oil-Based MWCNT-TiN Composite Nanofluids
item.description:
Abstract
To improve the volumetric solar absorption capability of the working fluid in direct absorption solar collectors (DASC) and to extend its application to medium- and high-temperature solar-thermal utilization, mono multiwalled carbon nanotube (MWCNT) nanofluids and MWCNT-TiN hybrid nanofluids were prepared using Therminol 66 heat-transfer oil as the base fluid by a two-step method. Unlike previous MWCNT-TiN studies mainly based on aqueous systems, this work introduces the hybrid absorber into a low-polarity heat-transfer oil medium and employs oleic-acid-assisted dispersion and ultrasonication to improve particle dispersion in the oil phase. The optical and photothermal conversion performances of MWCNT nanofluids were first evaluated. The results show that the addition of MWCNTs substantially enhances solar absorption; the average transmittance of the nanofluid decreased from 68.43% for the base fluid to 33.44%, and the maximum apparent photothermal conversion efficiency reached 82.51% at 10 ppm MWCNT. TiN nanoparticles were then introduced into the optimized MWCNT nanofluid to prepare MWCNT-TiN hybrid nanofluids. The hybrid nanofluids exhibited further enhanced absorption in the visible–near-infrared range. At a TiN concentration of 10 ppm, the MWCNT-TiN hybrid nanofluid achieved the highest apparent efficiency of approximately 88.48%, which was 5.97 percentage points higher than that of the 10 ppm MWCNT nanofluid. This enhancement is mainly attributed to the strengthened broadband absorption in the visible–near-infrared region after TiN incorporation; this behavior is consistent with the reported plasmonic absorption characteristics of TiN, although the efficiency improvement is not attributed solely to a single LSPR mechanism. Supplementary stability evaluation of the optimized 10 ppm MWCNT–10 ppm TiN nanofluid showed that the UV–vis absorbance retention after 10 and 20 thermal cycles was approximately 98.0% and 95.5%, respectively. The particle-size distribution showed a Z-average of 66.533 nm, a PDI of 0.125, and a main peak at 75.529 nm, indicating good short-term optical and dispersion stability. This study provides a reference for the selection and application of oil-based hybrid nanofluids in medium- and high-temperature DASC systems.

item.title: Carbide Slag-Assisted Steam Gasification of Sewage Sludge for Hydrogen-Rich Syngas Production and Heavy Metal Stabilization
item.description:
Abstract
Carbide slag (CS), a Ca-rich industrial residue, was investigated as a calcium source for enhancing steam gasification of sewage sludge (SS) and mitigating heavy metal risks in bottom residues. Gasification performance and heavy-metal behavior across Ca/C ratios and temperatures were assessed using apparent retention, Community Bureau of Reference (BCR) sequential extraction, the toxicity characteristic leaching procedure (TCLP), and the risk assessment code (RAC). At 700 °C, increasing Ca/C from 0 to 0.75 raised the H2 volume fraction from 57.73 to 68.02 vol %, H2 yield from 207.40 to 332.85 mL g–1, and cold gas efficiency from 28.09 to 42.24%. CS addition increased the apparent retention of Zn, Pb, and Cd and was accompanied by redistribution from the F1/F2 fractions toward the F3/F4 fractions and by lower TCLP leaching concentrations; the RAC risk levels of Zn and Cd decreased from high to medium. However, CS was largely ineffective for As immobilization because its apparent retention, BCR fraction distribution, and TCLP leaching behavior changed only slightly, while As remained at medium RAC risk. At Ca/C = 0.50, increasing temperature from 650 to 800 °C increased H2 yield and cold gas efficiency but decreased the H2 volume fraction and H2/CO ratio. Higher temperature reduced the potential mobility and TCLP leachability of metals retained in the collected bottom residues but decreased the apparent retention of Zn, Pb, Cd, and As. Overall, under the investigated conditions, Ca/C = 0.50 and 700–750 °C provided a representative compromise between hydrogen-rich gas production, CS dosage, operating-temperature requirements, and the environmental response of the collected bottom residues.

item.title: Degradation Behavior of NBR Seals Exposed to Halogenated Olefins under Coupled Thermal and Mechanical Loads: A Multiscale Experimental and Computational Study
item.description:
Abstract
Halogenated olefins are promising low-GWP substitutes for traditional halocarbons in refrigeration, fire protection, and energy storage, but their compatibility with elastomeric seals poses a potential safety risk in process systems. This study systematically investigates the degradation behavior of nitrile butadiene rubber (NBR) exposed to five representative halogenated olefins-namely, 2-bromo-3,3,3-trifluoropropene (2-BTP), 2-chloro-3,3,3-trifluoropropene (R1233xf), 2,3,3,3-tetrafluoropropene (R1234yf), cis-1,3,3,3-tetrafluoropropene (R1234ze(Z)), and trans-1,3,3,3-tetrafluoropropene (R1234ze(E))-under simulated service conditions (0–70 °C, 0–2000 N compressive load, 15–45 days). Overall, the performance evolution of NBR exhibits a strong dependence on environmental conditions, and is closely correlated with the molecular architecture of halogenated olefins. 2-BTP caused the most severe damage (compression set: 31.18%; hardness loss: 14.38%; compressive strength loss: 41.35%), while fluorinated olefins showed weaker effects. Microscopic and spectroscopic analyses confirmed surface roughening, microcracking, halogen penetration, and formation of C–X (X = F, Cl, Br) bonds. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed that thermal energy weakens intermolecular interactions, whereas compressive stress induces chain orientation and free-volume redistribution, synergistically enhancing diffusion. The diffusion coefficients follow R1234ze(E) > R1234yf > R1234ze(Z) > R1233xf >2-BTP. Density functional theory calculations confirm that halogen radicals attack NBR’s C═C and −CN groups via low-barrier pathways. These findings elucidate the degradation mechanisms of NBR seals and provide practical engineering guidance for material selection and failure prevention, contributing to safer process design with halogenated olefins.

item.title: Multi-Isotope Signatures in Modern Pig Bones: Evaluating Dietary and Hydrological Controls on Provenance in South Korea
item.description:
Abstract
Multi-isotope analysis of animal tissues is a powerful tool for provenance studies; however, its application to modern livestock is complicated by the widespread use of manufactured feed and managed water sources. In this study, we investigated the mechanisms by which dietary and hydrological isotope signals are incorporated into modern pig bone tissues and evaluated whether bone collagen (BC) and phosphate (BP) preserve interpretable provenance information. 87Sr/86Sr, δ13C, δ15N, and δ18O values were measured in pig bone, BC, and BP collected from 17 livestock farms across South Korea. Bone isotope compositions were compared with corresponding feed and groundwater values to assess the transfer of dietary and hydrological signals into skeletal tissues. Bone 87Sr/86Sr ratios ranged from 0.70991 to 0.72280 and largely overlapped with feed values (0.71009–0.71226), whereas groundwater values differed significantly from bone values (p < 0.0001), indicating that Sr incorporation was more strongly influenced by diet than by drinking water. However, the relative contributions of feed, groundwater and other sources were not quantified for source apportionment. δ13CBC values ranged from −17.6‰ to −13.4‰, and δ15NBC values ranged from 0.74‰ to 5.31‰. Both isotopic systems were significantly enriched relative to feed (p < 0.0001), with mean offsets of 1.69‰ and 1.72‰ for δ13C and δ15N, respectively. Both δ18OBC and δ18OBP were positively correlated with δ18OWater, although BP exhibited relatively stronger explanatory power (R2 = 0.61) than BC (R2 = 0.40). These results suggest that modern pig bones retain measurable dietary and hydrological isotope signals; however, the use of manufactured feed can possibly weaken or obscure local geological provenance signatures. Notably this study provides a multi-isotope baseline for pig farms in South Korea and highlights both the potential and limitations of skeletal isotope analysis for provenance investigations of modern livestock systems.

item.title: Experimental Study on Fracture Propagation and Seepage Variation Law under Alternating Injection Acid Fracturing Technology
item.description:
Abstract
This study targets the ultradeep, high-temperature, and high-pressure carbonate reservoirs in the Penglai Gas Area, Sichuan Basin. The existing acid fracturing technologies have ambiguous stimulation mechanisms and are difficult to regulate accurately. We conducted a series of physical experiments on the alternating injection of gelled acid and drag-reducing acid, aiming to optimize acid fracturing techniques and improve the reservoir stimulation performance. Dolomite cores collected from the Dengying formation were used as rock samples. With a true triaxial hydraulic fracturing simulation system, we designed four groups of alternating injection cycles and different mixing ratios of the gelled acid and drag-reducing acid. Combined with three-dimensional (3D) laser scanning technology to characterize the morphology of acid-etched fractures, parameters such as fracture roughness (JRC) and etching volume were quantitatively analyzed to explore the laws of fracture propagation, etching characteristics, and seepage variation under alternating injection conditions. The experimental results indicate that the second alternating cycle achieves the best acid etching and permeability improvement performance. By contrast, the fourth cycle produces insufficient etching and thus reduces the fluid flow capacity. The permeability enhancement capacity is the best when the ratio of gelled acid to drag-reducing acid is 7:3, and the excessive or insufficient proportion of gelled acid will reduce the etching heterogeneity and the permeability enhancement effect. Fracture morphology, etching degree, and JRC are the core factors determining seepage and permeability enhancement capacity. The tortuous (vertical + transverse) fracture has the optimal permeability enhancement potential, and the riverbed/groove etching morphology with a high JRC corresponds to higher seepage and permeability enhancement effects. This work clarifies the rules of fracture propagation and fluid flow evolution during alternating injection of acid fracturing. It provides experimental data and theoretical references for optimizing high-efficiency acid fracturing technologies for ultradeep carbonate reservoirs.

item.title: Interfacial Regulation of Hybrid Nanoparticles via Silane Modification and Corresponding Pore-Scale Flow Simulation
item.description:
Abstract
