Eight widely used group-contribution models were evaluated for their ability to estimate the isobaric heat capacity (Cp) of ionic liquids (ILs). A curated database containing 9037 experimental data points for 142 ILs, covering eight cation families, temperatures from 190 to 524.87 K, and heat capacities from 93.0 to 1805.7 J·mol–1·K–1, was assembled to assess model performance under diverse conditions. Three main evaluation criteria were applied: predictive accuracy, functional-group flexibility, and ability to represent structural diversity of cation–anion combinations. Among the evaluated models, “GAR”, “SOR”, and “MIA” exhibited the best predictive accuracy, with overall % AARD values of 5.10%, 4.30%, and 4.22%, respectively. The “MIA” model is particularly suitable for imidazolium- and pyridinium-based ILs, relevant in industrial contexts. The “SAT” model also proved promising for CAMD applications due to its flexible atomic-contribution framework. Overall, the study offers practical guidance for selecting group-contribution methods when experimental data are unavailable.

item.title: Neural Constrained Charge Equilibration for Extracting Charge Transport Parameters from Machine Learned Interatomic Potentials
item.description:
Abstract
Machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) continue to gain popularity as efficient tools for predicting energies and forces for atomic structures at an accuracy comparable to quantum chemistry. However, there are limited trained MLIPs for certain important applications such as in charge transport. Accelerating and automating the determination of parameters for such applications can be of critical importance in the rapid discovery of materials such as organic electronics (e.g., OLEDs). This work develops and introduces neural constrained charge equilibriation (NcQEq) and applies the technique to AimNet2 and OrbMol-V2. The new method enables extracting information about the diabatic states and thereby charge transport parameters. The approach is demonstrated on model systems against constrained density functional theory charge transport and then tested on intramolecular hole transport properties for polyethylene. This work demonstrates that the NcQeq approach is compatible with the charge equilibration schemes for AimNet2 and the latent charge predictions of OrbMol-V2. After calibration to reference data, the method enables estimation of the electronic coupling, reorganization energy, and the free energy difference.

item.title: Cadmium Exposure Aggravates SREBP-1c-Mediated Hepatic Steatosis and Liver Injury in High-Fat Diet-Fed Mice
item.description:
Abstract
Cadmium (Cd) is a persistent environmental heavy metal that bioaccumulates and is associated with diverse toxicities. Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is highly prevalent, and steatotic metabolic stress may increase vulnerability to toxicological insults. In this study, we used a free fatty acid (FFA)-treated hepatocyte model and high-fat diet (HFD)-fed steatotic mice to characterize hepatic responses to a short-term CdCl2 toxicological challenge under lipid overload conditions. In FFA-treated QSG-7701 cells, CdCl2 exposure was associated with increased lipid droplet accumulation, elevated oxidative stress, and increased apoptosis. In HFD-fed steatotic mice, short-term CdCl2 administration was associated with worsened liver injury and greater hepatic lipid accumulation compared with parallel steatotic controls. These phenotypic changes were accompanied by increased expression of lipogenesis-related markers, including SREBP-1c and SCD1, consistent with enhanced lipogenic signaling under steatotic stress. CdCl2 exposure was also associated with increased α-SMA and TGF-β, consistent with early fibrogenic activation in this short-term model rather than staged fibrosis. Rapamycin-treated mice exhibited attenuation of multiple injury- and lipid-related readouts compared with parallel CdCl2-treated groups, supporting its use as a pharmacological probe in this acute setting. Collectively, these observations support a model in which short-term CdCl2 challenge aggravates steatotic liver injury under lipid overload.

item.title: Comparative Feasibility Assessment of a Simplified Mossel EE–MacConkey Workflow for Detection of Enterobacteriaceae in Selected Non-Sterile Pharmaceutical Products
item.description:
Abstract
Microbiological quality control of nonsterile pharmaceutical products requires reliable detection of Enterobacteriaceae while maintaining operational feasibility in routine laboratory settings. Harmonized pharmacopoeial methods involve sequential procedures, including pre-enrichment, selective enrichment, and differential isolation. These steps increase analytical time and resource requirements. In this study, a simplified culture-based workflow consisting of pre-enrichment in Tryptic Soy Broth, selective enrichment in Mossel Enterobacteria Enrichment broth, and isolation on MacConkey agar was comparatively evaluated against harmonized pharmacopoeial procedures. The assessment was performed using Escherichia coli (ATCC 8739) and Salmonella typhimurium (ATCC 14028) inoculated into finished pharmaceutical products (pravastatin sodium and erlotinib tablets) and a raw material (paracetamol). Qualitative recovery of target microorganisms was observed in the evaluated finished products under both workflows. Comparable qualitative recovery patterns were observed under the experimental conditions evaluated. The simplified approach reduced total analysis time from six to 4 days and decreased estimated culture media costs from USD 340.25 to USD 95.99 per analysis. No recovery of E. coli was observed in paracetamol samples under either workflow. Neutralization also failed to restore microbial growth, suggesting potential matrix-associated inhibitory effects. Within the defined experimental scope, the proposed approach proved practically applicable to the evaluated matrices. However, the study was limited to two finished pharmaceutical products and one pharmaceutical raw material. Therefore, broader applicability requires further evaluation across a wider range of pharmaceutical matrices.

item.title: The Buffer Illusion: How TRIS and HEPES Enhance Bioactivity of Bioglass 45S5
item.description:
Abstract
In vitro tests of glass, glass-ceramic, or ceramic biomaterials such as synthetic hydroxyapatite (HA) and β-tricalcium phosphate (β-TCP) are performed using simulated body fluid (SBF), in which the pH is maintained using TRIS buffer (ISO standard 23317:2014; recently updated as ISO standard 23317:2025). When evaluating the experiments, we not only looked at the tested material itself but also analyzed the SBF leachate. We have found out that TRIS buffer, as well as other tested buffers (Good’s buffers), actively interacts with glass and ceramic materials. They significantly accelerate their dissolution (up to 3× higher compared to unbuffered SBF). This increases the local supersaturation of biogenic ions near the surface and promotes the formation of the expected hydroxyapatite (the newly formed hydroxyapatite layer is labeled as HAp). In this work, we focused on bioglass 45S5 to observe the corrosion rate of the glass surface on samples in the form of bulk, in SBF solutions buffered with (i) TRIS and (ii) HEPES, and we used (iii) SBF without any buffer for comparison. The glass corrosion rate and the growth kinetics of the new HAp layer (SEM/EDS, XRD, FTIR) were compared with the results of the leachate analyses (pH, ICP-OES). The concentration of SiIV in the leachates showed the corrosive effects of each of the solutions, while the concentrations of Ca2+ and (PO4)3– confirmed precipitation of a new Ca–P phase. The results confirmed earlier findings and showed that the TRIS and HEPES buffering systems are not inert and are strongly corrosive to bioglass 45S5. Moreover, their parts incorporate into the newly formed Ca–P layer and change its quality and crystallinity. These findings suggest that the current approach to in vitro testing of these materials requires reconsideration.

item.title: Comparison of the Photodegradation of Pharmaceuticals and Personal Care Products (PPCPs) in Water and Ice
item.description:
Abstract
Photochemical reactions are prevalent in natural aquatic environments and play a crucial role in aquatic ecosystems. Sunlight-induced photodegradation is particularly effective in degrading various pharmaceuticals and personal care products (PPCPs). However, the photochemical behavior of pollutants within surface ice in cold regions remains unclear. This review synthesizes current research advances regarding the photochemical transformation mechanisms and associated environmental risks of PPCPs in ice, highlighting the significance of these transformations in evaluating the environmental impact of PPCPs in such contexts. In ice or snow, PPCPs may undergo transformation pathways (e.g., photolysis and free radical reactions), which differ from those in aquatic environments. Factors including ice crystal structure, pH, dissolved organic matter, and light conditions can influence their transformation efficiency and the resulting degradation products. This review systematically elucidates the photochemical reaction pathways, key influencing factors, and potential ecotoxicological effects of PPCPs in ice. These transformation processes may generate secondary products that are more persistent or toxic than the parent compounds, posing potential threats to aquatic ecosystems and food chains in cold regions. Therefore, there is an urgent need to thoroughly explore the environmental behavior and ecological risks of PPCPs to provide a scientific basis for pollution control and ecological protection in cold environments.

item.title: Spray-Coated Macroporous CaCO 3 –PVA Structures for Radiative Cooling
item.description:
Abstract
Current dielectric composites require coating normally thicker than 400 μm to produce the radiative cooling effect, compared to 50–100 μm for standard paints. In this study, CaCO3–PVA composite coatings with thicknesses below 300 μm are produced, forming macro-porous yet smooth structures. Controlled ball milling of CaCO3 produces uniformly distributed micro- and nanosized particles with optimized sizes for solar radiation backscattering. To produce a favorable material structure, optimized particle sizes are spray-coated to construct the composites. The composite has macro pores and micro particles of CaCO3 with PVA as a stable binding and coating agent. Optical and scanning electron microscopy confirms uniform particle dispersion and macropore formation across coating thicknesses. The coatings exhibit strong thickness-dependent reflectivity, achieving over 95% solar reflectivity for 290 μm thickness, while maintaining emissivity of ∼90% in the 8–13 μm atmospheric window. Raman spectroscopy verifies that no significant chemical or structural changes to CaCO3 occur during fabrication. Based on measured spectral, indoor solar simulator tests, environmental and typical solar irradiation data for hot climate conditions, modeling predicts an average subambient temperature reduction of approximately 3–6 °C. These results demonstrate that CaCO3–PVA composites provide a cost-effective, scalable, and NIR-absorption-free alternative to conventional white cooling paints, with strong potential for practical, large-scale passive cooling applications.

item.title: Physics-Informed Multi-Parameter Optimization of Oxide-Based Memristor Characteristics Using Genetic Algorithms
item.description:
Abstract
We present a multiobjective, physics-informed optimization framework for oxide-based memristive devices that jointly minimizes forming voltage (Vf) and maximizes memory contrast (HRS/LRS). The proposed approach integrates COMSOL Multiphysics with MATLAB through a genetic algorithm (GA), enabling self-consistent electrothermal simulations and systematic exploration of a high-dimensional design space encompassing geometrical, electrical, thermal, and operational parameters. By optimizing 13 key variables, the GA efficiently identifies optimal trade-offs between switching efficiency and resistance ratio. The optimization results demonstrate a substantial enhancement in device performance, with the high-resistance-state to low-resistance-state ratio (HRS/LRS) improved by up to 21× relative to the reference device, while alternative optimized configurations achieve a reduction in Vf down to 0.7× of the reference value. A parameter-importance analysis based on a random forest model highlights oxide thickness and effective electrical and thermal conductivities as influential parameters. Importantly, the optimization further reveals nontrivial multiparameter trade-offs, demonstrating that reductions in Vf and enhancements in HRS/LRS can be simultaneously achieved through coordinated tuning of geometrical, material, and pulse-related parameters beyond simple intuitive design rules. Overall, the MATLAB–COMSOL co-optimization strategy provides a scalable and generalizable computational design methodology for next-generation low-power, high-contrast RRAM devices, and offers quantitative insights into the coupled physical mechanisms underlying filament formation and rupture.

item.title: Corrosion Resistance of Boronized Carbon Steel in a Galinstan–Refrigerant Two-Phase Agitated System
item.description:
Abstract
This study experimentally evaluates, for the first time, the corrosion resistance of boronized carbon steel in environments containing liquid Galinstan (GaInSn) and selected organic refrigerants (n-pentane and R1233zd(E)) at 150 °C for up to 80 days. The tests simulated gas–liquid-metal two-phase exposure under pseudodynamic conditions, where the test coupons and corrosive media were mechanically agitated. These conditions are relevant to advanced liquid-metal heat-transfer systems. Cross-sectional microstructural analysis revealed a uniform 180–200 μm thick FeB–Fe2B bilayer coating exhibiting a distinctive sawtooth morphology associated with strong adhesion to the substrate. Optical microscopy, hardness determination, and ICP-OES analysis indicated that the iron boride coating maintained its structural integrity after exposure. No evidence of surface degradation (e.g., cracking, caverns, peeling) or substrate degradation was observed by the employed characterization techniques. The coating thickness and microhardness showed no systematic decrease after exposure, remaining at their original levels. ICP-OES analysis revealed negligible concentrations of boron and iron (0.01–0.03 wt %) in the exposed Galinstan, with no systematic increase. Collectively, these observations indicated that no significant degradation or dissolution of the iron boride coating was detected during up to 80 days of exposure under the investigated conditions. In contrast, previously reported studies of SS316 identified measurable degradation under comparable conditions after only 20 days. These findings suggest that iron boride coatings warrant further investigation as a potentially cost-effective material option for selected liquid Galinstan-based heat-transfer systems. Additional studies involving larger sample populations, higher temperatures, longer exposure durations, and true dynamic flow conditions are required to further assess long-term performance and application potential.

item.title: Laminar Flame Speeds of Premixed Dimethoxymethane/Air Flames at Elevated Temperatures and Pressures
item.description:
Abstract
The world’s increasing energy demand combined with the continuous depletion of fossil fuel reserves and growing interest in reducing greenhouse gas emissions has spurred research on new alternative fuels that can partially satisfy the energy demand while mitigating air pollution. In this regard, dimethoxymethane (DMM), an oxygenated fuel that can be produced from renewable sources, is a promising alternative fuel that can be used in diesel blends in combustion engines. This research presents DMM laminar flame speed measurements of outwardly propagating flames, which were carried out in an optically accessible constant-volume chamber at several temperatures (373, 423, and 473 K) and pressures (1, 3, and 5 bar), for equivalence ratios from 0.7 to 1.7. The experimental results were compared against one-dimensional laminar premixed flame simulations from Converge CFD using detailed kinetic mechanisms. At 1 bar, the maximum DMM laminar flame speeds were found to be 63.4, 77.5, and 91.8 cm/s at 373, 423, and 473 K, respectively, at an equivalence ratio of 1.2. At 373 K and 3 and 5 bar, the maximun flame speeds were 49.8 and 43.2 cm/s at equivalence ratios of 1.2 and 1.1, respectively.

item.title: Structure Determination of a Single Bioapatite Crystal from an Archeological Metastatic Cancer Bone – a TEM Case Study
item.description:
Abstract
The inorganic component of bone, bioapatite, is generally regarded as a poorly crystalline, carbonate-substituted hydroxyapatite. However, a direct structural and chemical characterization of bioapatite has not yet been achieved due to the extremely small size of its crystals ─ typically only a few tens of nanometers ─ and their intimate association with the organic matrix of bone. In this study, we examined a single crystal of bioapatite extracted from an archeological, metastatic bone cancer sample using 3D ED (3-Dimensional Electron Diffraction), which enabled structural analysis of the three-dimensional reciprocal space despite the nanometric crystal dimensions. Conventional structural techniques, such as single-crystal X-ray diffraction, require crystals several orders of magnitude larger than those found in bone, rendering them inapplicable to individual bioapatite crystallites. Powder-based methods, on the other hand, can only provide averaged structural information across billions of crystals, obscuring the intrinsic structural features of individual nanocrystals. The bioapatite single crystal was found to crystallize in space groups P63 and P63/m, with lattice parameters a = 9.414 Å; c = 6.881 Å, and showed no evidence of carbonate substitution. The measured Ca/P ratio on single crystals was 1.65 on average.

item.title: NHC-Au-Xanthate Complexes: Selective Cytotoxic Activity and Mechanistic Insights
item.description:
Abstract
In this study, a series of NHC-Au-xanthate (NHC-Au-Xa) complexes was evaluated for their antiproliferative activity and mechanism of action. Molecular docking studies identified thioredoxin reductase (TrxR) as a plausible molecular target and suggested that the inhibitory potency may depend on the ability of the complexes to position the gold center in close proximity to the catalytic selenocysteine residue. Consistent with this hypothesis, the investigated compounds induced TrxR inhibition, leading to an intracellular redox imbalance, enhanced reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, increased release of damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs), including HMGB1, and activation of both apoptotic and necrotic cell death pathways. The aforementioned mechanism might indicate the engagement of immunologically relevant cell death responses. Additionally, fluorescence studies demonstrated the preferential accumulation of a representative complex in cancer cells compared with normal fibroblasts. In conclusion, these findings provide new insights into the mechanism of action of NHC-Au-xanthate complexes and highlight their potential as redox-active anticancer agents with possible chemoimmunotherapeutic relevance.

item.title: Fine Assessment of Water Abundance and Water Inflow Potential in Coal-Bearing Strata Based on Water Storage Space Microelements
item.description:
Abstract
Mine water inflow is one of the primary hazards threatening the safety of coal-mining production. Groundwater in coal-bearing strata serves as the direct water-filling source for coal mining, and its water abundance significantly impacts the intensity of the mine water inflow. The coal-bearing strata in the Ordos Basin, China, were formed during the Jurassic period, and the coal measure sandstones are characterized by short diagenetic times, weak cementation, and significant variations in the water abundance. This paper analyzes the paleosedimentary environmental characteristics of the coal-bearing strata in the study area, revealing the distribution of sedimentary facies and their water-controlling rules. Combining cast thin section (CTS) and nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) analyses, the porosity, pore structure, and connectivity characteristics of sandstones with different grain sizes were investigated. Utilizing fractal theory, the coal-bearing strata were three-dimensionally discretized to obtain water storage space microelements. By statistically analyzing the proportions of sandstones with varying grain sizes within the microelements and integrating porosity characteristics, the comprehensive water storage space of the microelements was derived. Finally, based on the sandstone water storage microelements, a three-dimensional evaluation of water abundance and an assessment of water inflow potential in the coal-bearing strata were conducted. The results indicate that sandstone aquifers are widely developed within the sedimentary paleochannels in the study area, exhibiting strong water abundance and excellent connectivity, thus serving as dominant runoff channels for groundwater. The porosities of coarse, medium, and fine sandstones were 21.07%, 17.31%, and 10.2%, respectively. The water storage space of the microelements within the coal-bearing strata ranges from 600 to 1700 m3, peaking at 1400–1700 m3 within the 20–40 m and 80–100 m horizons above the coal seam roof, which are classified as strong water-rich zones. The water abundance evaluation based on water storage microelements demonstrates high consistency with the exploration results derived from 3D seismic multiattribute fusion; based on this, a fine assessment model for water inflow potential was established. The research findings provide a novel methodology for predicting water abundance and evaluating the water inflow potential in weakly cemented coal-bearing strata.

item.title: Water-Soluble Au–NHC Complexes for Aqueous A 3 Coupling: Ligand Architecture, Catalyst Speciation, and Reuse
item.description:
Abstract
The development of water-soluble gold catalysts for reactions in water remains challenging because catalyst speciation and oxidation-state changes can strongly influence activity and stability. Herein, two water-soluble Au(III)–NHC complexes (2a–b)–selected for their distinct structural features–were synthesized and evaluated in the A3-coupling reaction in aqueous media, together with their corresponding Au(I) precursor. Among the Au(III)–NHC precatalysts 2a and 2b, complex 2b displayed superior activity compared to 2a, affording quantitative yields at 1 mol % and maintaining significant conversion even at 0.2 mol % loading. Steric analysis based on %VBur calculations showed that, upon Au–Cl bond cleavage, the sulfonate side chain in 2b cyclized and coordinates to the metal center, leading to a significant increase in buried volume. Recycling experiments showed progressive deactivation of both Au(III) precatalysts, while NMR monitoring in the presence of phenylacetylene provided evidence for changes in Au(III)/Au(I) speciation, including formation of Au(I) species. Addition of catalytic amounts of CuCl2 improved the recycling of 2b, although catalyst reuse remained limited to three cycles. These results establish a correlation between ligand-controlled steric modulation, oxidation-state stability, and catalytic performance in aqueous Au(III)–NHC systems for the multicomponent A3-coupling reaction.

item.title: Alterations in Coal Permeability and Adsorption Capacity Post Oxidation Treatment: Insights into Enhancing Coalbed Methane Production
item.description:
Abstract
Organic matter dissolution by oxidants can enhance the coal permeability. However, as coalbed methane (CBM) is predominantly reserved in the adsorbed state, the organic matter dissolution changes the adsorption–desorption equilibrium, thus affecting the CBM production. Current studies have not sufficiently addressed the combined variations in permeability and adsorption capacity after oxidation, which are critical for enhancing CBM production via oxidation. Experiments on coal permeability, molecular structures, adsorption capacity, wettability, and pores were conducted. The results demonstrated that new pores and fractures were formed after oxidation, as evidenced by an average increase in porosity of 15.57%, leading to an average increase of 161.16% in the initial permeability (k0, at atmospheric pressure). However, the increased pore size and oxygenated functional group content lead to a decreasing contact angle (CA) and specific surface area (SSA), ultimately causing an average reduction in adsorption capacity of 72.20%. Changes in k0/CA were negatively correlated with moisture content (Mad) + ash yield (Ad) and positively correlated with fat/oxygenated functional group (FA/OFG). The decreasing CA indicates significantly enhanced hydrophilicity, inhibiting depressurization by drainage, and negatively affecting CBM production. The change in k0/the change in CA after oxidation generally exceeds 10 when Mad + Ad < 14% and FA/OFG > 0.5, which is favorable for CBM production enhancement under similar treatment conditions in this study. These findings determine the coals to be more suitable for oxidation with equal treatment and offer insights for assessing the CBM production enhancement potential via oxidation.

item.title: 6-Chloropyridinyl Benzoate Fragments as Selective Anti-Melanoma Scaffolds Triggering ROS-Mediated Mitochondrial Apoptosis
item.description:
Abstract
Fragment-like molecules represent valuable starting points in anticancer drug discovery due to their structural simplicity and favorable physicochemical properties. In this context, the combination of phenotypic drug discovery (PDD) with fragment-based drug discovery (FBDD) offers an effective strategy for the rapid identification of bioactive scaffolds. Herein, a small in-house library of 6-chloropyridinyl benzoate fragments was designed to explore the antiproliferative potential of this underexplored scaffold. The compounds were first evaluated in silico, confirming favorable physicochemical and ADME profiles consistent with fragment-like chemical space, and were subsequently synthesized through simple one-pot procedures. Phenotypic screening against a panel of human cancer cell lines (A-375, HCT-116, and MCF-7) revealed a selective antiproliferative effect toward melanoma cells. Two derivatives, 7d and 7k, emerged as the most active compounds, displaying low micromolar activity against A-375 cells (IC50 = 1.59 ± 0.07 μM and 1.08 ± 0.03 μM, respectively) and high selectivity (SI > 60) compared to noncancerous 16-HBE cells. Mechanistic investigations demonstrated that these fragments induce apoptosis through an ROS-dependent mitochondrial pathway, associated with mitochondrial dysfunction and cell cycle arrest at the G1–S transition. Density functional theory (DFT) analysis further suggested that the enhanced electrophilic character and electron-accepting ability of the most active derivatives may contribute to their biological activity. Overall, this study identifies chloropyridinyl benzoate fragments as a previously unexplored scaffold with selective antimelanoma activity and highlights their potential as promising starting points for fragment-to-lead optimization.

item.title: Study on the Application of Recycled Polyester Fibers in Stone Matrix Asphalt Mixtures
item.description:
Abstract
In order to study the effect of recycled polyester fiber on the road performance of the SMA asphalt mixture, a method of improving the road performance of asphalt concrete by recycled polyester fiber/lignin fiber composite was proposed. By using the method of 1:1 compounding of recycled polyester fiber and lignin fiber in the SMA-13 mixture, the optimum gradation and optimum asphalt-aggregate ratio of the mixture under the compounding ratio were determined by the Marshall test. The optimum mixing process of the composite fiber was determined, and the road performance of the mixture under the conditions of no fiber, recycled polyester fiber/lignin fiber 1:1 composite, and 0.3% lignin fiber addition was compared. Through a high-temperature rutting test, immersion Marshall test, low-temperature bending test, and four-point bending fatigue test, the mechanical properties of SMA asphalt concrete and the improvement effect of road durability were comprehensively evaluated and verified. The experimental results show that compared with the SMA asphalt mixture without fiber and 0.3% lignin fiber, the high-temperature rutting resistance of the composite fiber SMA asphalt mixture is obviously improved and the recycled polyester fiber can improve the low-temperature crack resistance, fatigue deformation, and water stability of the asphalt mixture. When the ratio of recycled polyester fiber to lignin fiber is 1:1, the dynamic stability of SMA asphalt concrete is 1.1 times that of the single addition of lignin fibers. The maximum flexural strength of the specimen at low-temperature failure is increased by 12%, and the fatigue life is increased by 24%. Lignin fiber increases the thickness of the oil film through adsorption, while recycled polyester fiber enhances adhesion, reinforcement, and the interface effect. By integrating adsorption stability with reinforcement bridging and load transfer, the stability of asphalt concrete under temperature changes, water damage, and stress is strengthened, thereby further improving the durability of the SMA pavement.
